title: Conditional Sentences
objectives: Identify the four main types of Greek conditions
Form future more vivid with ἐάν + subjunctive

grammar.explanation: Greek conditions are classified by their protasis (if-clause) and apodosis (then-clause). The mood and tense indicate how the speaker views the condition: real, likely, possible, or contrary to fact.
rules: εἰ + indicative = factual or assumed true
εἰ + past indicative (with ἄν in apodosis) = contrary to fact

exercises.question: What type? εἰ ἦλθες, εἶδες ἄν αὐτόν.
exercises.answer: Contrary-to-fact past (aorist indicative + ἄν): 'If you had come, you would have seen him.'

exercises.question: Translate: ἐὰν μείνητε ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τῷ ἐμῷ, ἀληθῶς μαθηταί μού ἐστε.
exercises.answer: If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples.

readingPassage.greek: Ἐὰν ἀγαπᾶτε με, τὰς ἐντολὰς τὰς ἐμὰς τηρήσετε. Εἰ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἦτε, ὁ κόσμος ἂν τὸ ἴδιον ἐφίλει. Εἰ ὧδε ἦς, οὐκ ἂν ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός μου.
readingPassage.translation: If you love me, you will keep my commandments. If you were of the world, the world would love its own. If you had been here, my brother would not have died.
